facts.statement: Anodontosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: taxon: Anodontosaurus

facts.statement: The genus Anodontosaurus was named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1928.
facts.quote: Anodontosaurus was named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1928

facts.statement: The name was inspired by compression damage to the holotype that removed the teeth, misleading the original describer.
facts.quote: It was inspired by the fact that compression damage to the specimen had removed the teeth

facts.statement: Remains of Anodontosaurus are also known from the Dinosaur Park Formation, dating to approximately 75.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: and is also known from the Dinosaur Park Formation (75.6 Ma ago)

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurid reaching up to 4 to 5 meters in length and 2 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Anodontosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurid, measuring up to 4 - 5 m in length and 2 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus was a quadrupedal, ground-dwelling herbivore.
facts.quote: It was a quadrupedal, ground-dwelling herbivore

facts.statement: The skull of Anodontosaurus features postocular caputegulae, small polygonal bone plates located immediately behind the eye.
facts.quote: The skull features postocular caputegulae, which are small polygonal plates of bone that are present on the cranium and are situated to the immediate rear of the eye

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus is estimated to have measured 6.5 meters in length, 2 meters in height, and weighed 2.5 tons.
facts.quote: Se calcula que medía 6,5 metros de largo unos 2 m de alto y pesaba 2,5 toneladas

facts.statement: In 1986, Coombs determined that specimen AMNH 5266, previously referred to Euoplocephalus, represented a juvenile Anodontosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1986 Coombs examined specimen AMNH 5266, at the time by him referred to Euoplocephalus, and determined that it was a juvenile

facts.statement: Specimen AMNH 5266 was discovered in 1912 at the Red Deer River and collected by Barnum Brown with assistance from Peter Kaisen, George Olsen, and Charles M. Sternberg.
facts.quote: AMNH 5266 was discovered in 1912 at Red Deer River and was collected by Barnum Brown with assistance from Peter Kaisen, George Olsen, and Charles M Sternberg

facts.statement: Victoria Arbour argued that Anodontosaurus is distinct from Euoplocephalus based on differences in skull ornamentation, cervical half-ring ornamentation, and tail club morphology.
facts.quote: Victoria Arbour considered Anodontosaurus distinct from Euoplocephalus in distinctive skull and cervical half ring ornamentation, as well as tail club morphology

facts.statement: The scientific validity of the genus Anodontosaurus was formalized through three separate studies.
facts.quote: The validity of Anodontosaurus was formalized in three studies

facts.statement: Victoria Arbour and Philip Currie formally revalidated the genus Anodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Arbour along with Philip Currie formalized the revalidation of Anodontosaurus

facts.statement: A specimen from the Dinosaur Park Formation was later designated the holotype for the new species Anodontosaurus inceptus.
facts.quote: The DPF specimen, however, was later made the holotype of a new species, A. inceptus

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus inceptus is a subdivision of the genus described by Penkalski in 2018.
facts.quote: subdivision: Anodontosaurus inceptus Penkalski, 2018

facts.statement: The genus Anodontosaurus was named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1928 based on the holotype specimen CMN 8530.
facts.quote: Anodontosaurus fue nombrado por Charles Mortram Sternberg en 1928, basándose en el holotipo CMN 8530

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was collected by Sternberg in 1916 from a quarry of the Canadian Museum of Nature, located about 13 kilometers southwest of Morrin.
facts.quote: Este esqueleto aplastado fue recolectado por Sternberg en 1916 en una cantera del Museo Canadiense de la Naturaleza, a unos 13 kilómetros al suroeste de Morrin

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the upper part of the Horse Canyon Formation, dating from the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian, approximately 71 to 70.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue extraído de la parte superior de la Formación Cañón Herradura, de la unidad 2, que data de entre finales del Campaniano hasta principios del Maastrichtiano hace unos nos 71 a 70,2 millones de años

facts.statement: The name was inspired by compression damage to the specimen that had removed its teeth, leading Sternberg to mistake them for crushing plates.
facts.quote: El nombre fue inspirado por el hecho de que los daños por compresión de la muestra le había quitado los dientes

facts.statement: The species name lambei honors Lawrence Morris Lambe, a Canadian geologist and paleontologist at the Geological Survey of Canada where the holotype is housed.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, lambei, honra a Lawrence Morris Lambe, el geólogo y paleontólogo canadiense del Servicio Geológico de Canadá en el que se aloja el fósil holotipo

facts.statement: Following a redescription of Dyoplosaurus, Victoria Arbour argued in 2010 that Anodontosaurus is a valid genus distinct from Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, tras la redescripción de Dyoplosaurus como un género válido por Arbour et al. (2009), Victoria Arbour (2010) señaló que Anodontosaurus es un taxón válido también y distinto de Euoplocephalus

facts.statement: Arbour noted that Anodontosaurus differs from Euoplocephalus in skull features, mid-cervical ring ornamentation, and tail club morphology, including the presence of triangular, pointed, and blunt osteoderms.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con su estudio, publicado solo como un resumen, Anodontosaurus difiere de Euoplocephalus en características del cráneo y de la ornamentación del anillo medio cervical, así como la morfología de la maza ósea de la cola, incluyendo la presencia de osteodermos triangulares, en punta y romos en Anodontosaurus

facts.statement: A specimen from the Dinosaur Park Formation, TMP 1997.132.1, was reassigned to Anodontosaurus, extending the genus's stratigraphic range.
facts.quote: En un estudio basado en los resultados de su resumen SVP 2010, Arbor junto con Philip Currie formalizaron la revalidación de Anodonotsaurus, y un espécimen de la Formación del Parque Dinosaurio, TMP 1997.132.1, se remitió a Anodontosaurus extendiendo el rango estratigráfico del género unos millones de años atrás

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie formalized the revalidation of Anodontosaurus, noting that a specimen from the Dinosaur Park Formation extended the genus's stratigraphic range.
facts.quote: Arbor junto con Philip Currie formalizaron la revalidación de Anodonotsaurus, y un espécimen de la Formación del Parque Dinosaurio, TMP 1997.132.1, se remitió a Anodontosaurus extendiendo el rango estratigráfico del género unos millones de años atrás

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie formalized the revalidation of Anodontosaurus, assigning a Dinosaur Park Formation specimen to the genus and extending its stratigraphic range.
facts.quote: Arbor junto con Philip Currie formalizaron la revalidación de Anodonotsaurus, y un espécimen de la Formación del Parque Dinosaurio, TMP 1997.132.1, se remitió a Anodontosaurus extendiendo el rango estratigráfico del género unos millones de años atrás

facts.statement: The Dinosaur Park Formation specimen was later designated as the holotype of a new species, A. inceptus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el espécimen de DPF se convirtió en el holotipo de una nueva especie, A. inceptus

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus belongs to the subfamily Euoplocephalini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Euoplocephalini

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Anodontosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The time range for Anodontosaurus is from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Anodontosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 14
